command:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
# #997 MIGRATION — MIG-10b. THE SUPERSESSION. Rollback for every file touched here was captured in
# MIG-10a with digests, and the replacement runtime is already serving on the canonical port.
#
# Only the Ollama portion of compose is removed. postgres, redis, open-webui and portainer keep
# their definitions, their volumes and their published ports exactly as they were.
#
# open-webui is repointed at http://host.docker.internal:11434 -- measured, not assumed: from inside
# the container that URL returned the model list while the LAN address 192.168.88.9:11434 timed out
# and the Hyper-V address 172.25.208.1:11434 refused. Docker Desktop proxies host.docker.internal
# from a component running on the host itself, so it reaches a 127.0.0.1-bound listener. That is the
# whole reason loopback-only and a working web UI are not in conflict here.
#
# NOTE: no `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway` is added. On Docker Desktop the name is
# built in and resolves to 192.168.127.254; mapping it to host-gateway would instead point it at the
# bridge gateway 172.18.0.1, which cannot reach the host's loopback. The "portable" line would break
# the thing it looks like it is protecting.

$compose = 'C:\HermesLab\hermes\docker-compose.yml'
$start = 'C:\HermesLab\hermes\start-hermes.ps1'

Write-Output '--- PRE-STATE ---'
Write-Output "compose_sha256=$((Get-FileHash $compose -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower())"
Write-Output "start_sha256=$((Get-FileHash $start -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower())"
docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}|{{.Status}}|{{.Ports}}' 2>&1
Write-Output '--- INFERENCE-PROXY-CONTEXT ---'
# A separate compose project (williamos-hermes-agent) that has been Exited(255) since 00:48Z. Not
# this lane's to start or fix, but its restart policy decides whether it reappears at the reboot
# acceptance test, so record it rather than be surprised by it.
docker inspect williamos-hermes-inference-proxy --format '{{.State.Status}} restart={{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}} project={{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project"}}' 2>&1
docker inspect ollama --format 'ollama status={{.State.Status}} restart={{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}}' 2>&1

$newCompose = @'
# Hermes core stack. Boring and stable on purpose.
# Start:   ..\start-hermes.ps1   (or: docker compose up -d)
# Status:  docker compose ps
# Logs:    docker compose logs -f <service>
# Stop:    docker compose down   (data persists)
#
# Storage note: C: is nearly full, so the big files (Ollama model weights) live on
# D:\HermesData\ollama. The small services use named volumes (fine on C:).
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OLLAMA IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS FILE  (#997)
#
# Ollama on HERMES is owned by ONE canonical Windows service definition:
#   scheduled task  WilliamOS-HERMES-Ollama   (SYSTEM, at startup, no execution time limit)
#   startup path    C:\HermesLab\hermes\ollama-service\hermes-ollama-service.ps1
#   listens         127.0.0.1:11434  (loopback only)
#   models          D:\HermesData\ollama\models   (the same store this file used to bind)
#   GPU             Tesla P40 by UUID, in TCC mode, capped at 150 W on every boot
#
# It is not a container because it cannot be one on this host. The P40 runs in TCC mode, TCC devices
# have no WDDM presence, and WSL2 reaches GPUs only through the WDDM stack. NVML enumerates every
# adapter before answering any query, so nvidia-container-cli's prestart hook fails for EVERY card
# here -- asking for only the RTX 3050 fails exactly as hard as asking for the P40. That is why the
# old ollama container exited 128 and never came back.
#
# DO NOT re-add an ollama service here. Two owners of port 11434 and one model store is the failure
# #997 was commissioned to end. To roll the whole change back, see C:\HermesLab\hermes\_997-rollback.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
    container_name: postgres
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
    ports:
      - "5433:5432"   # host 5433 -> container 5432 (host 5432 is already in use)
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7
    container_name: redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes"]
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redisdata:/data

  open-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    container_name: open-webui
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    environment:
      # Was http://ollama:11434 over this project's bridge network. Ollama now runs on the Windows
      # host bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Docker Desktop proxies host.docker.internal through a
      # component on the host, so this reaches the loopback listener -- verified from inside this
      # container, while the LAN address timed out. Do NOT add an extra_hosts host-gateway mapping:
      # that would repoint this name at the bridge gateway, which cannot reach host loopback.
      OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://host.docker.internal:11434
    volumes:
      - webuidata:/app/backend/data
    # depends_on: ollama  -- removed with the service. Ollama's availability is now the Windows
    # service's business, and open-webui already tolerates the backend being down at start.

  portainer:
    image: portainer/portainer-ce:latest
    container_name: portainer
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - portainerdata:/data

volumes:
  pgdata:
  redisdata:
  webuidata:
  portainerdata:
'@
Set-Content -Path $compose -Value $newCompose -Encoding UTF8

$newStart = @'
# Brings the Hermes core stack up. Run from anywhere:
#   C:\HermesLab\hermes\start-hermes.ps1
#
# Ollama is NOT part of this stack (#997). It is a Windows service definition -- scheduled task
# WilliamOS-HERMES-Ollama, started at boot, bound to 127.0.0.1:11434, Tesla P40 only. This script
# reports on it but does not own it, so that there is exactly one owner and it is obvious which.
#
# -PullImages is opt-in ON PURPOSE. This script used to run `docker compose pull` unconditionally,
# which silently replaced whatever image identity was actually running with whatever :latest had
# become that day -- image preservation depended on nobody using the documented start path. Pulling
# is now something you ask for.
param([switch]$PullImages)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$here = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
Set-Location $here

# The model store. Owned by the Windows Ollama service; created here only so a fresh machine does
# not fail confusingly.
$modelDir = "D:\HermesData\ollama"
if (-not (Test-Path $modelDir)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $modelDir | Out-Null
    Write-Host "Created $modelDir"
}

# Ensure .env exists.
if (-not (Test-Path ".\.env")) {
    Copy-Item ".\.env.example" ".\.env"
    Write-Warning "Created .env from template. Edit it and set a real POSTGRES_PASSWORD, then re-run."
    exit 1
}

if ($PullImages) {
    Write-Host "Pulling images (this REPLACES the running image identity with :latest)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    docker compose pull
} else {
    Write-Host "Using the images already present (pass -PullImages to update them)." -ForegroundColor Cyan
}

Write-Host "Starting stack..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
docker compose up -d

Write-Host "`nStatus:" -ForegroundColor Green
docker compose ps

Write-Host "`nOllama (Windows service, not a container):" -ForegroundColor Green
$task = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "WilliamOS-HERMES-Ollama" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (-not $task) {
    Write-Warning "  scheduled task WilliamOS-HERMES-Ollama is NOT registered -- open-webui will have no models."
    Write-Host "  install: powershell -File .\ollama-service\install-hermes-ollama-service.ps1"
} else {
    Write-Host "  task state: $($task.State)"
    try {
        $tags = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags" -TimeoutSec 5
        Write-Host "  serving $($tags.models.Count) model(s) on 127.0.0.1:11434"
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "  task is registered but 127.0.0.1:11434 did not answer: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        Write-Host "  log: C:\ProgramData\WilliamOS\logs\hermes-ollama-service.log"
    }
}

Write-Host "`nOpen:" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "  Open WebUI : http://localhost:3000"
Write-Host "  Portainer  : http://localhost:9000"
Write-Host "`nPull a model:  D:\HermesServices\ollama\v0.9.2\ollama.exe pull <model>   (OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434)"
'@
Set-Content -Path $start -Value $newStart -Encoding UTF8

Write-Output '--- POST-EDIT-DIGESTS ---'
Write-Output "compose_sha256_after=$((Get-FileHash $compose -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower())"
Write-Output "start_sha256_after=$((Get-FileHash $start -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower())"

Write-Output '--- COMPOSE-VALIDATES ---'
docker compose -f $compose --project-directory 'C:\HermesLab\hermes' config --services 2>&1
Write-Output "config_rc=$LASTEXITCODE"

Write-Output '--- REMOVE-HAND-CREATED-CONTAINER ---'
# Hand-created 2026-08-18T20:42:32Z outside compose, carrying restart=unless-stopped. Left in place
# it would be restarted by the Docker daemon at the next boot and fight the Windows service for
# port 11434 -- which is precisely what the acceptance test is looking for. The image is NOT removed:
# ollama/ollama@sha256:9d30908e4114... stays in the local image store so the rollback is real.
docker rm ollama 2>&1
Write-Output "rm_rc=$LASTEXITCODE"
docker image inspect ollama/ollama:latest --format 'image_preserved={{.Id}}' 2>&1

Write-Output '--- RECONCILE-STACK ---'
docker compose -f $compose --project-directory 'C:\HermesLab\hermes' up -d 2>&1
Write-Output "up_rc=$LASTEXITCODE"
Start-Sleep -Seconds 12
docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}|{{.Status}}|{{.Ports}}' 2>&1

Write-Output '--- OPEN-WEBUI-REACHES-OLLAMA ---'
docker inspect open-webui --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' 2>&1 | Select-String 'OLLAMA_BASE_URL'
$r = docker exec open-webui python3 -c "import urllib.request,json
d=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen('http://host.docker.internal:11434/api/tags', timeout=8))
print('models', len(d['models']), sorted(m['name'] for m in d['models']))" 2>&1
Write-Output "from_open_webui => $($r -join ' | ')"

Write-Output '--- STILL-LOOPBACK-ONLY ---'
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 11434 -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 80
$c = New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient
try { Write-Output "lan_192.168.88.9_11434=$(if ($c.ConnectAsync('192.168.88.9', 11434).Wait(2500) -and $c.Connected) { 'CONNECTED' } else { 'refused' })" } catch { Write-Output 'lan_192.168.88.9_11434=refused' } finally { $c.Close() }

Write-Output '--- ONE-OWNER-CHECK ---'
Write-Output "containers_named_ollama=$((docker ps -a --filter name=^/ollama$ --format '{{.Names}}' 2>&1) -join ',')"
Get-Process -Name 'ollama*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { "host_process pid=$($_.Id) path=$($_.Path)" }
Write-Output "task_state=$((Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'WilliamOS-HERMES-Ollama').State)"
Write-Output '--- MODELS-INTACT ---'
$b = Get-ChildItem 'D:\HermesData\ollama\models\blobs' -File | Measure-Object -Sum Length
Write-Output "blobs=$($b.Count) bytes=$($b.Sum)"
Write-Output '--- RC ---'
